svg.text: MPx Orb: Drop-in Ferrofluid Capture Ball

A small magnetic ball carrying ferrofluid. Drop it in any bottle and shake: the oily magnetic layer grabs floating microplastics and the magnet keeps it all on the ball. Pull it out, wipe, re-coat, reuse.

g.text: Ferrofluid spikes poke through the
shell holes and grab passing plastics.
Tether clips to the cap
pull the ball out, no fishing
Food-safe steel cord
or silicone, swaps between bottles
Shake about 30 s
every shake pushes water
past the ball again
Ø 18–20 mm ball
fits a standard bottle neck
(about 21 mm inside)
Drop it in, shake, then pull it out by the tether: the plastics come out stuck to
the ball instead of going down your throat.
Why a shell around the fluid?
Shaking would tear loose ferrofluid off a bare magnet
and leave oil in the water. The shell lets water through
but keeps the fluid in; the magnet pulls back any drops.
Dose
≈ 0.25 mL oil + a pinch of Fe₃O₄ per 500 mL bottle,
the same per-litre dose as [1] (0.5 mL oil per litre).

Repeat with a fresh coat for the next bottle.
D · Clean and re-coat, and what to check

g.text: The used towel is a test sample
Rinse the oil off the towel with a solvent, collect what is left on
a membrane, stain it with Nile Red and count it on MPx Detect.
That tells you how much plastic one bottle actually contained.
Refill pot:
food-grade oil + Fe₃O₄, mixed in the ratio from [1];
one pot re-coats the ball many times.

svg.text: Untested set-up. [1] and [2] spread ferrofluid or iron particles
through the water and pulled them out with an outside
magnet. Fluid held on a small ball has not been tested.
Short reach. A small magnet's pull fades within millimetres,
so only water that passes through or near the ball is
treated. More shaking means more passes.
No oil left behind. Use food-grade oil; after use, check the
Magnet safety. Fully sealed so it can't rust; keep away from
young children, as swallowed magnets are dangerous.
Capture only. It does not kill germs.

g.text: [1] Hamzah, S. et al. (2021). Synthesis, characterisation and evaluation on the performance of ferrofluid for microplastic removal from synthetic and actual wastewater. J. Environ. Chem. Eng. 9, 105894.
[2] Grbic, J. et al. (2019). Magnetic extraction of microplastics from environmental samples. Environ. Sci. Technol. Lett. 6(2), 68–72.
